basis: Defining vascular and skin lesions; pulmonary AVMs and hepatic AVMs/portal hypertension each 30-79%. Oral lesions omitted at cap; anemia is secondary blood loss.

decisions.haematologic: none: blood-loss anemia is a separately diagnosed consequence, rather than direct disease of blood cells or marrow.
decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary AVMs with functional shunting occur in 30-79%; recurrent nasal mucosal bleeding adds support.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: cutaneous hemorrhagic telangiectasias are defining lesions, present in 80-99%.

basis: Vitamin A excess is a nutritional metabolic disorder; damaging skin, liver and skeletal manifestations vary across acute and chronic presentations.

decisions.dermatologic: none: persistent epithelial injury is characteristic of chronic toxicity, but a frequency of at least 30% across this umbrella is not established.

basis: Small-intestinal mucosal injury defines the disease; nutritional anemia is a separately diagnosable consequence. An infectious cause remains unproven.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: presumed postinfectious pathogenesis and antibiotic responsiveness do not establish an infection or immune-mediated disease.

basis: The poisoning itself is defined by gastrointestinal mucosal injury, myelosuppression and alopecia; occasional hand-foot syndrome adds no additional axis.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: alopecia is explicitly included among the poisoning's defining toxicities; hair is covered by this axis.

basis: Breast duct origin has no axis, but the defining erosive, crusting lesion directly damages the overlying epidermis.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent epidermal erosion and crusting characterize the lesion itself; this is direct skin damage despite its breast duct origin.

basis: Systemic vasculopathy and pulmonary injury define it; inflammatory muscle injury with weakness affects ~50%, and peripheral neuropathy ~32-55%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: sensory neuropathy ~55%, with direct axonal injury ([cohort](https://ehp.niehs.nih.gov/doi/pdf/10.1289/ehp.111-1241614)).
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: muscle injury with weakness affects ~50%; inflammatory myopathy is documented ([pathology](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1654352/)).

basis: Retroperitoneal stromal origin is outside the specified axes; no locomotor tissue origin or covered-organ invasion is established. Inflammatory infiltrates do not establish immune disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: retroperitoneal fibroblastic tissue is not connective tissue of the locomotor system; soft-tissue histology alone does not establish this axis.

basis: Primary skeletal muscle degeneration; neuropathic EMG patterns do not by themselves establish nerve injury. Cardiomyopathy occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: none: EMG axonal/neuropathic annotations occur in 30-79%, but do not establish direct peripheral nerve damage in this primary muscular dystrophy.

basis: Down syndrome causes neurodevelopmental impairment; congenital heart defects ~40-50%, hearing impairment ~50-75%, and functional ocular abnormalities >50%.

decisions.ocular: involved: developmental ocular abnormalities causing impaired visual function affect over 50%, beyond characteristic facial appearance.
decisions.otologic: involved: persistent hearing impairment affects approximately 50-75% and is a common functional manifestation of the syndrome.

basis: COACH defines cerebellar disease and hepatic fibrosis; nephronophthisis with renal failure in 2/2; strabismus and ptosis each in 1/2. Secondary anemia excluded.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus and ptosis each occur in 1/2 reported patients and affect ocular alignment or eyelid function; oculomotor apraxia itself is neurologic.
